title: The goddess says: I am Brahman
hook: all the gods ask the goddess who she is, and her answer is why so many Hindus call God Ma
carry: the goddess is Brahman itself, not a sidekick

segments.voice: Yesterday: the mind is nature's dance; the self is the watcher. Samkhya's dancer shows herself, and once she's been fully seen, she stops.

Who are you? It's the question you ask a stranger at the door, a new neighbor, a voice on the phone. In a short text called the Devi Upanishad, it's the question every god asks the goddess. They come and stand before her, all of them together, and ask: who are you, great goddess? Yesterday, in Samkhya, nature danced and said nothing. Today she is asked to speak for herself. And her answer isn't a name, or a family, or a list of victories.
screen: `ALL THE GODS COME TO HER.` → `WHO ARE YOU, GREAT GODDESS?` → `TODAY SHE SPEAKS.`

segments.voice: Here's her answer, in paraphrase. I am of the very nature of Brahman. From me comes this world, made of prakriti and purusha, nature and spirit. I am joy and not-joy. I am knowing and not-knowing. First, she answers with Brahman, the one ultimate reality the Upanishads point to. Not a goddess beside God. The goddess says: that's me. Second, the pair. Yesterday Samkhya kept prakriti and purusha apart, the dancer and the watcher. Here both come from her. She is the dance and the one watching it. Third, the opposites. Joy and not-joy, knowing and not-knowing. She doesn't keep only the comfortable half. In Shakta eyes, that's why the same Devi can be gentle Lakshmi on a lotus and fierce Kali with a sword: one power, many faces. Fourth, the gods bow and praise her. This is the heart of Shakta Hinduism, one of the tradition's great streams: the highest reality is worshipped as the Goddess, the Mother. It's why so many Hindus simply call God Ma, why pilgrims climbing to the shrine of Vaishno Devi call out Jai Mata Di, victory to the Mother, and why Navaratri gives nine nights to her. Not everyone on the Hindu path puts it this way. Vaishnava and Shaiva traditions name the highest reality Vishnu or Shiva. But in this Upanishad, the goddess answers for herself. Today: when someone hears goddess and pictures a sidekick, this text is the answer. Ask her who she is, and she doesn't give a husband's name. She says: everything.
screen: `I AM OF THE NATURE OF BRAHMAN.` · `PRAKRITI AND PURUSHA, BOTH FROM HER.` · `ONE POWER, MANY FACES.` · `GOD AS MA.` · then, large: `WHO ARE YOU? I AM BRAHMAN.`

segments.voice: Notice one comfortable thing right now, warmth or a soft seat, and hold it for a few breaths. Then notice one uncomfortable thing, a tight shoulder or a worry, and hold that too, without pushing it away, letting both sit in the same space the way the goddess holds joy and not-joy. If you pray, you can rest in the name of the Devi, or the name you use for God; if you don't, rest in the space that holds both.
Shakti as a philosophy. In the Devi Upanishad, the gods ask who she is, and she answers: of the nature of Brahman, the source of prakriti and purusha both.
Your line: the goddess is Brahman itself, not a sidekick. Asked who she is, she answers with everything. I'll be here tomorrow.

howItsDone: The Devi Upanishad, also called the Devi Atharvashirsha, is chanted by worshippers of the goddess, including during Navaratri, and is studied as a statement of the goddess as ultimate reality.
